messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: AUTH_SERVICE_TOKEN_VALIDATION_FAILURES high error rate (>= 95th percentile)
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert AUTH_SERVICE_TOKEN_VALIDATION_FAILURES fired -> escalated to on-call (jamie). Incident ID: PD-78910
jamie (oncall): acked. I'm looking. tagging @sara_auth and @mike_infra.
jamie (oncall): initial check: control plane logs show a bunch of 500s from /v1/token/validate starting ~2935002400. Rate ~1200rps -> 500s. Customers reporting sign-in failures.
kate_support: seeing multiple support tickets with 401/500 for OAuth flows, around EMEA. Some customers hit for admin APIs.
sara_auth: jumping in. Checking signer service (token-signer). Last deploy ~2934980000. JWKS published to auth-service cache at 2934999000 according to deploy logs.
mike_infra: infra side: no CPU/GPU saturation on signer nodes. Network health ok. No scaling events.
sara_auth: getting errors in auth-service when fetching JWKS: 404 for kid mismatch on some keys. Logs: `ERROR fetch_jwks: got 200, no matching kid in keys for kid=0x8f3a`
leo_platform: we have an automated fallback path that should accept legacy keys for 10m if signer unresponsive. Looks like it didn't trigger. Investigating policy config.
jamie (oncall): can we temporarily enable permissive fallback? If we can accept older key id for a short window that should reduce customer impact.
sara_auth: I can flip the config on auth-service to broaden accepted kids for 5m. Pushing patch now. Command: ``kubectl -n auth patch configmap auth-jwks-policy -p '{"data":{"allow_legacy_kids":"true"}}'``
jamie (oncall): please post ETA and rollback plan.
sara_auth: patch applied. Restarting auth pods (rolling). `kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n auth`
mike_infra: restart looks healthy - pods coming back 3/3. Monitoring error rate.
leo_platform: error rate dropped ~75% in the last 30s. Good signal.
kate_support: customers reporting reduced failures. Still seeing some 401s for long-lived tokens.
sara_auth: investigating those 401s. Might be cache TTL mismatch between signer and auth-service. Signer rotated keys at 2934998800 but auth-service cached old keys with TTL=10m; some machines still served stale cache. We'll tighten propagation.
jamie (oncall): what's the root cause hypothesis?
sara_auth: preliminary: key rotation happened and signer published new JWKS with new kid. A subset of auth-service instances didn't refresh their JWKS cache due to a bug combined with a conservative TTL config. When requests hit instances with stale cache the kid didn't match -> validation failures. Fallback policy should have allowed secondary verification but didn't due to a config regression in the canary from last week.
mike_infra: confirmed config regression: a helm diff showed `allow_legacy_kids=false` got merged into canary values. That prevented the fallback.
leo_platform: mitigation steps done: 1) Enabled permissive acceptance (5m) 2) Forced JWKS cache refresh across all auth-service instances with `kubectl exec` script to curl signer/.well-known/jwks.json and update cache 3) Reverted canary config that disabled fallback
jamie (oncall): can we push a stronger guard so future rotations don't break like this?
sara_auth: yes. Action items: a) add a pre-rotation hook to verify all auth-service pods can fetch and match new kid b) add a propagation check that fails key rotation if <95% pods report the new kid c) change default TTL to 30s for JWKS cache in auth-service and add jitter
mike_infra: I'll own the rollout of the pre-rotation hook and CI check. Putting a ticket: PLAT-1282.
jamie (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 18 minutes. @mike_infra please own incident until EOD. If anything regresses page SRE.
kate_support: captured customer impact: ~120 customers saw transient auth failures, 7 enterprise customers hit persistent errors and were escalated to AE. Notifying account teams.
sara_auth: post-mitigation: validation errors are back to baseline. No 500s for token validation in last 5m. I'll keep a watch for 1 hour and then run the rotation replay to validate the pre-rotation checks.
leo_platform: adding incident note and timeline to the incident tracker. Will attach logs: `s3://redwood-incident-logs/2935002468/`
jamie (oncall): thanks team. Quick retrospective items: document rotation runbook, add canary gating for fallback configs, monitor JWKS propagation metric (new).
mike_infra: confirmed ownership. Escalation route tested. Closing PD alert.
incident-bot: Incident PD-78910 acknowledged by jamie (oncall). Status: mitigated.
kate_support: closing related support tickets with a summary and apology.
sara_auth: I filed follow-up PRs: auth#452 (cache TTL), auth#453 (pre-rotation check), infra#876 (canary gating).
leo_platform: final note: keep an eye on any auth-related spike for the next 24h. I'll schedule a 30m postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PT.
jamie (oncall): great work everyone :thumbsup:
